brief_ACCT61555:
RENEWAL BRIEF — ACCT61555 (Manufacturing, Enterprise/Monthly, $10,229 MRR, renews in 1 day)

HEALTH: At Risk — Save (churn risk 49.1%, expansion score 2.7%)

EVIDENCE: Seat utilization has collapsed to 7.3%, down 47.5% over the trailing 3 months -- this account has essentially stopped using the product. 10 support tickets in the last 3 months, 2 with negative sentiment. Monthly billing (no annual lock-in) and a renewal tomorrow make this urgent.

TALKING POINTS FOR THE CALL: Lead with genuine curiosity, not a pitch -- ask what changed operationally (team restructure? a champion who left? a competing tool?). Don't open with retention offers before understanding the cause; a utilization collapse this sharp is usually organizational, not pricing. If it's a champion-departure issue, ask to be introduced to the new stakeholder before the renewal date.

CONFIDENCE: High that this is a real save-motion priority (evidence is unambiguous); confidence in root cause is Low until the call happens.
brief_ACCT60113:
RENEWAL BRIEF — ACCT60113 (Education, Enterprise/Monthly, $9,962 MRR, renews in 1 day)

HEALTH: At Risk — Save (churn risk 46.2%, expansion score 2.5%)

EVIDENCE: Utilization at 19.8%, down 7.9% over 3 months -- consistently low, not a sudden drop. 10 support tickets in the trailing 3 months (0 flagged negative-sentiment, so support experience itself isn't the driver). NPS is a middling 48, not a detractor score.

TALKING POINTS: This profile (chronically low usage, decent NPS, high ticket volume) suggests a rollout/adoption problem more than dissatisfaction -- the team may have bought more seats than they've operationalized. Consider offering a focused re-onboarding session rather than a discount; a price concession doesn't fix an adoption gap.

CONFIDENCE: Medium-High on the risk signal; the adoption-gap hypothesis is a reasonable read of the evidence but should be confirmed on the call.
brief_ACCT60338:
RENEWAL BRIEF — ACCT60338 (Retail, Enterprise/Monthly, $10,260 MRR, renews in 1 day)

HEALTH: At Risk — Save (churn risk 44.1%, expansion score 2.1%)

EVIDENCE: Utilization at 22.5% but actually UP 11.9% over the trailing 3 months -- this is a low-but-improving signal, distinct from ACCT61555's collapse. Only 2 support tickets, none negative.

TALKING POINTS: This account is likely climbing out of a slow start rather than heading for the door -- the model still flags it as at-risk because the absolute utilization level is low, but the trend is the more important number here. Frame the call around accelerating the ramp (a check-in on rollout progress, offer training resources) rather than a save conversation.

CONFIDENCE: Medium -- the risk score is real but the positive trend meaningfully softens it; worth a lighter-touch outreach than the two accounts above.
brief_ACCT61399:
RENEWAL BRIEF — ACCT61399 (Retail, Enterprise/Monthly, $9,315 MRR, renews in 1 day)

HEALTH: At Risk — Save (churn risk 47.4%, expansion score 2.9%)

EVIDENCE: Utilization at 34.4%, down 18.1% over 3 months. 2 support tickets, both negative-sentiment -- a small volume but a 100% negative rate is notable. NPS 67 (a strong promoter score), which is an unusual combination with active churn-risk signals.

TALKING POINTS: The NPS/usage-decline mismatch is the story here -- a genuinely happy customer whose usage is falling off suggests an internal change (reorg, budget review, project ending) rather than product dissatisfaction. Worth a direct, low-pressure check-in: "noticed usage has dipped, wanted to check in" rather than a retention pitch.

CONFIDENCE: Medium -- the high NPS is a meaningfully positive counter-signal the model doesn't have a clean way to fully offset against the usage decline; treat the risk score as a prompt to investigate, not a verdict.
brief_ACCT61397:
RENEWAL BRIEF — ACCT61397 (Media, Enterprise/Monthly, $9,114 MRR, renews in 1 day)

HEALTH: At Risk — Save (churn risk 47.3%, expansion score 2.6%)

EVIDENCE: Utilization at 31.6%, UP 26.4% over the trailing 3 months -- a meaningfully improving trend despite the risk flag. 2 tickets, 1 negative.

TALKING POINTS: Similar profile to ACCT60338 -- low absolute utilization but a strong positive trend. The model's risk score weighs the low absolute level heavily; the trajectory suggests this is a ramping account, not a churning one. Recommend monitoring rather than urgent save-motion outreach; a light "how's the rollout going" touchpoint is enough for this renewal.

CONFIDENCE: Medium-Low that this needs urgent intervention -- flagged for completeness, but the trend data argues against treating it with the same urgency as the collapsing-usage accounts above.
brief_ACCT61112:
RENEWAL BRIEF — ACCT61112 (Healthcare, Enterprise/Annual, $9,466 MRR, renews in 60 days)

HEALTH: Growth Opportunity (expansion score 88.8%, churn risk 5.3%)

EVIDENCE: Utilization at 80.3% and climbing (+6.2% over 3 months) -- this account is running close to its seat cap with sustained growth. Only 2 support tickets, none negative. Churn risk is negligible.

TALKING POINTS FOR THE CALL: This is a seat-expansion conversation, not a renewal-risk conversation. Lead with their growth ("looks like your team's really adopted this") and ask directly about headcount plans for the next 2 quarters -- accounts running this hot on utilization typically hit a hard capacity wall within 1-2 quarters if not proactively expanded. Bring a seat-tier upgrade proposal to the renewal call itself rather than waiting for them to hit the ceiling and file a support ticket about it.

CONFIDENCE: High -- both the utilization level and trend point the same direction, and the low support-ticket/risk profile removes the usual 'are they actually happy' caveat.
brief_ACCT61207:

brief_ACCT60347:
RENEWAL BRIEF — ACCT60347 (Software, Enterprise/Monthly, $9,489 MRR, renews in 1 day)

HEALTH: Growth Opportunity (expansion score 85.6%, churn risk 21.6%)

EVIDENCE: Utilization at 82.0%, up 7.0% over 3 months -- a genuinely strong, growing account. But: 10 support tickets in 3 months (2 negative) and an NPS of -4 (a detractor). This is the most internally-contradictory profile in this batch: heavy, growing usage paired with real dissatisfaction signals.

TALKING POINTS: Do NOT lead with an expansion pitch here despite the utilization number -- address the NPS detractor status and recent negative support interactions first. An account this engaged that's also unhappy is a bigger long-term risk than a quiet low-usage account, because they have the leverage (and reason) to churn loudly or negotiate hard at renewal. Get a support/success leader on this call, not just a growth-motion rep.

CONFIDENCE: High that this needs a different conversation than a standard expansion pitch -- the model's quadrant label ('Growth Opportunity') undersells the real complexity here, which is exactly why the evidence table matters more than the label alone.
brief_ACCT61105:
RENEWAL BRIEF — ACCT61105 (Financial Services, Enterprise/Annual, $9,154 MRR, renews in 60 days)

HEALTH: Growth Opportunity (expansion score 87.8%, churn risk 9.9%)

EVIDENCE: Utilization at 78.0%, up 8.5% over 3 months. 20 support tickets in the trailing 3 months (2 negative) -- the highest ticket volume in this batch, though the negative rate (10%) is proportionally low given the volume, and likely reflects a large, active user base generating routine requests rather than dissatisfaction.

TALKING POINTS: High-touch account -- confirm with the support team whether the ticket volume is routine (config requests, permissions, integrations) or symptomatic before the call. If routine, this is a strong expansion candidate given sustained high utilization and low churn risk; consider proposing a dedicated support/success contact as part of an upgraded tier, which financial-services accounts at this size often value independent of the expansion pitch itself.

CONFIDENCE: Medium-High on expansion; recommend a quick support-log review before the call given the ticket volume, even though the negative-sentiment rate itself isn't alarming.
